question.text: Photoelectrons are emitted when <math><mn>4000</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Å</mi></math> radiation is incident on a surface of work function <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math>. These photoelectrons pass through a region having <math><mi>α</mi> </math> -particles to form <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ion, emitting a single photon. In this process, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions thus formed are in their fourth excited state. The energy released during the combination of <math><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math> ions is

options.text: 5.38 eV
3.38 eV
2.38 eV
1.38 eV
